source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Monitor and document baseline environmental conditions before industrial activity commences.

3. Conduct regular air quality testing using calibrated and certified equipment, ensuring adherence to national and international standards.

4. Identify pollutants of interest to monitor based on the types of industrial emissions prevalent in the area (e.g., particulates, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, volatile organic compounds, carbon monoxide, and heavy metals).

5. Set up continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) where available and feasible, to collect real-time data around the clock.

6. Use a combination of stationary and portable monitoring devices such as high-volume samplers, optical particle counters, and gas analyzers.

7. Establish a grid of monitoring stations around the periphery of the industrial site to capture emissions in different wind directions and accurately estimate their dispersion.

8. Validate monitoring devices periodically using known standards and conduct regular maintenance to ensure accuracy and precision.

9. Maintain an inventory of emission sources, accounting for point sources
